trialCurve.yUnit: fraction of rounds striking a 6 ft x 100 ft board
trialCurve.note: Scharnhorst's Prussian trials: 92, 64, 65, 42, 26, 19 hits per 200 rounds at 100-600 paces on a board 6 ft x 100 ft (pp. 80-83, as reproduced on secondary web pages; original not read). Pace taken as 0.75 m (assumption). The point at 0 m is extrapolated. Chosen over the often-quoted 60/40/25/20% table (Picard, via Hughes), which a web check showed was shot from a fixed rest at a 1.75 m x 3 m target, not at a formation front.

battlefieldFactor.note: Scales trial hits to battle. Gives 1.8% of rounds at 75 m and 1.4% at 135 m. Anchors: Hughes's Albuera estimate of about 1.3 casualties per 100 shots (secondary, search snippet), inside his overall span of under 1 to over 15; and the prototype's 1.8% at its engagement range. The design draft's '3-5%' could not be supported. The most influential single assumption in the model.

roundsPerMinute.note: Commonly given as 2-3 at first and 1-2 sustained; a web check found no reliable source. One flat figure until the fouling rule exists. Prototype reload of 3.2 s x7 gives 2.7.

reloadJitter.note: Each reload varies by plus or minus this fraction.

trialCurve.yUnit: fraction of rounds striking a 6 ft x 100 ft board
trialCurve.note: Same curve as the French musket. Scharnhorst rated the French musket best at 100 paces and the English first or equal beyond (secondary, search snippet), but the per-pattern rows could not be found, so no difference is modelled.

openFireRange.note: Prototype musket range of 95 px x1.4. Consistent with volleys opened at 100-150 paces (Muir, from memory).

arcHalfAngle.note: A line or column fires at targets within this angle of its facing (0.7 rad).

moraleFloor.note: Fire effect is multiplied by floor + (1 - floor) x morale/100.

vsArtillery.note: Gun crews are a dispersed target.

vsColumn.note: Shots that miss the front ranks of a column find the ranks behind.

artilleryTargetPenalty.note: When choosing a target, a battery counts as this much farther away (30 px x1.4).

lookRange.note: A halted unit turns to face the nearest enemy within this distance (240 px x1.4).

rankAndFileShare.note: Share of a battalion's strength carrying a musket in the ranks; the rest are officers, sergeants, drummers and file-closers. The prototype's line fired with 0.9 of its men.

openingStagger.note: Units' first volleys and salvos are spread at random over this long, so that a whole line does not fire on the same second. The prototype staggered first volleys over 3 s (x7 = 21 s).

field_8pdr.label: Field gun of the 6- to 9-pounder class (French 8-pdr or 6-pdr, British 9-pdr)

roundshotCurve.yUnit: fraction of rounds striking a cloth target 6 ft x 30 ft
roundshotCurve.note: Müller's 6-pdr trials: 100% at 520 yd, 31% at 950 yd, 17% at 1,200 yd (as quoted on a secondary web page; original not read). The last point is extrapolated.

roundshotBattlefieldFactor.note: Trial to battle reduction for roundshot. With six guns and a three-deep line this gives 4.5 men per salvo inside 475 m; the prototype gave 7 falling to 4.5.

roundshotMaxRange.note: A little beyond Müller's last trial range.

roundshotEffectiveRange.note: British 9-pdr about 800 yd (secondary web page). Used by the battery's decision to advance and by target scoring.

roundshotReload.note: Prototype 5 s x7, i.e. 1.7 rounds a minute per gun. Gribeauval 8-pdr about 2 a minute (Wikipedia, search snippet).

menPerRank.note: An effective round strikes a man in about half the ranks it passes: 1.5 men on a three-deep line, 1 on a two-deep line.

maxRanksTraversed.note: Cap on penetration, so an enfiladed line suffers 2.7 x a three-deep line taken frontally (prototype 2.6 x).

squareTargetFactor.note: Roundshot treats a square as a target as deep as the battalion's column, times this. Prototype ratio of square to column loss, 3.2 / 2.4.

canisterRange.note: British practice was not to use case beyond about 350 yd (secondary web page, search snippet).

canisterHitsCurve.yUnit: hits per round on a trial screen
canisterHitsCurve.note: 'A 6-pdr could deliver 55 hits at 200 yd, only 6 at 600 yd' (historyofwar.org, test unnamed; search snippet). The points at 0 and 366 m are interpolated guesses.

canisterBattlefieldFactor.note: Trial to battle reduction for case. Chosen so a six-gun salvo at 180 m causes about 33 casualties on a line, the prototype's 34.

canisterReload.note: 2-3 rounds a minute is commonly stated; a web check found no source.

roundshotCurve.yUnit: fraction of rounds striking a cloth target 6 ft x 30 ft
roundshotCurve.note: Müller's 6-pdr curve stretched 1.25 x in range. Müller's own 12-pdr table could not be found.

roundshotEffectiveRange.note: 900-1,000 m (Wikipedia, Canon de 12 Gribeauval; search snippet).

roundshotReload.note: About one round a minute (Wikipedia, Canon de 12 Gribeauval; search snippet).

maxRanksTraversed.note: Heavier shot carries farther through a formation.

squareTargetFactor.note: Roundshot treats a square as a target as deep as the battalion's column, times this. Prototype ratio of square to column loss, 3.2 / 2.4.

canisterRange.note: 500-600 m depending on the source (Wikipedia; search snippet).

canisterHitsCurve.yUnit: hits per round on a trial screen
canisterHitsCurve.note: Large case of 41 balls (Wikipedia, Canon de 12 Gribeauval); the fall-off by range is a guess shaped like the 6-pdr figures.

aimTolerance.note: A battery fires only when pointed within this angle of its target (0.22 rad).

unlimberTime.note: Time halted before a battery that has moved may fire. Prototype 3 s x7 = 21 s; about a minute is commonly given for foot artillery. Unverified.

strengthJitter.note: Artillery salvo effect varies by plus or minus this fraction (prototype 0.7 + 0.6 x random).

reloadJitter.note: Each gun reload varies by plus or minus this fraction, as the musket's does.
